DEFINITIONS & POSSIBLE CASE
INDEPENDENT CLAUSE
DEPENDENT CLAUSE
1
They can exist alone.
I get annoyed...
IF people talk loudly.
2
They need another clause to exist.
I can’t stand it...
IF a child misbehaves.
3
Switching Clauses
If someone chews and talks,
I get nauseous.
There is also another way to construct the zero conditional
As we know, actions make other people react when they happen. When an event is the consequence of another one, we tend to use conditionals.
4
When people eat with their mouth open, my mum just loses it!
Jake hates it when someone smokes in public.

To Consider 
1. This Conditional sets actions that are real no possibilities no hypothesis.
2. It is the only conditional that can have the words IF and When switched because of the use it has..
3.  Zero conditional only works using the present tense.
4. Commas are needed if the dependent clause goes first.

slideDifferences.nativeText:
Conditionals may have a main purpose but they can receive a variety of functions.
Functions
Examples
1
Things that are generally true.
If my dad catches us eating his chocolate, we are grounded for weeks.
Dilan gets upset when someone smokes in a public area.
2
Facts or scientific statements
Water boils if it reaches 100 degrees.
The sea gets high tides  if the moon is in a further range than it regularly is.
3
Giving instructions
If you leave the room, turn the lights off.
Tell Jake to make his homework when you call him.
To consider 
When giving instructions, the independent clause is mainly used in imperative form.

texts: Conditionals may have a main purpose but they can receive a variety of functions.
If my dad catches us eating his chocolate, we are grounded for weeks.
Dilan gets upset when someone smokes in a public area.
Water boils if it reaches 100 degrees.
The sea gets high tides  if the moon is in a further range than it regularly is.

If you leave the room, turn the lights off.
Tell Jake to make his homework when you call him.
When giving instructions, the independent clause is mainly used in imperative form.

texts: So tell me Rose, what annoys you?
Well, if someone chews with their mouth open, that drives me crazy, Mandy.
I know! When someone eats and talks at the same time, I feel it so gross.
Don’t make me start  with nail biters!
Totally! When I see a kid doing it, I just can’t help it and tell his mum.
Wait! How about nose pickers? I hate it when I see someone picking their nose out.
I know! People need to get some good manners nowadays.
Indeed! And basic things like if you go out of a room, close the door behind you.
